subject: Setting legend title (although possibly with completely the wrong  idea)

messages.author: 87387836bb825314
messages.subject: Setting legend title (although possibly with completely the wrong  idea)
parts:
Hi,

I'm using the code below to plot a graph using ggplot 2:

windows()
allpixels <- read.table("D:/UserData/Robin Dissertation/For RSPSoc
Conf Paper/R/AllPixels_Resamp.txt", header=T)
lowest <- read.table("D:/UserData/Robin Dissertation/For RSPSoc Conf
Paper/R/Lowest30.txt", header=T)
bright_757 <- read.table("D:/UserData/Robin Dissertation/For RSPSoc
Conf Paper/R/bright_757_no_outliers.txt", header=T)
bright_1095 <- read.table("D:/UserData/Robin Dissertation/For RSPSoc
Conf Paper/R/bright_1095_no_outliers.txt", header=T)
bright_112 <- read.table("D:/UserData/Robin Dissertation/For RSPSoc
Conf Paper/R/B112_NoTree.txt", header=T)
graph <- qplot(B2, B3, data=allpixels, main="GCTs within SPOT feature
space", xlab="Band 2: Red", ylab="Band 3: NIR")
graph <- graph + geom_point(aes(B2, B3, color="Lowest Dark"),
data=lowest)
graph <- graph + geom_point(aes(B2, B3, color="Bright 757"),
data=bright_757)
graph <- graph + geom_point(aes(B2, B3, color="Bright 1095"),
data=bright_1095)
graph <- graph + geom_point(aes(B2, B3, color="Bright 112"),
data=bright_112)
graph

Originally I was setting the colour of each different plot series
outside of the aes(), but then realised that to get it to display on
the legend I had to put it within the aes(). Through trial and error I
have found that if I put the names I want in the legend there then
they will come up in the legend correctly.

However, how do I change the legend title? At the moment it is "Lowest
Dark", and I can't seem to change it at all. I have a feeling I might
have completely the wrong idea here, I feel that setting the colour in
the aes() call in the way I've done may be incorrect.

What would be the best way to do this? Basically, I have these four
data frames which I'm plotting from, and I want each one to come up in
a different colour, and be labelled on the legend.

Thanks in advance,

Robin
